selection_rule: PRE-COMMITTED before any sampled row was read: from judged.jsonl in file order, take rows at 0-based index i where i % 5 == 3 (the 167 / task-185 rule) — on this ONE-arm 50-row file that yields 10, so the sample was EXTENDED, before reading any row, by the phase-1 rows (i % 5 == 1) to reach the protocol's 20 items: indices 1,3,6,8,...,46,48. File index is the only selection key; question text, gold, answer, question_type and judge labels played no part in which rows were sampled.
scoring_protocol: Each item hand-scored EXACT / PARTIAL / WRONG from the question, the gold reference answer and the model answer ONLY, under the judge's own rubric (bench/memory/judge.mjs, judge-prompt.2): WRONG leads — an answer that does not state the gold fact is WRONG (refusals, 'not in my memory', a different fact or number); PARTIAL requires part of the gold fact on the table; EXACT states the gold fact, equivalent wording fine. The judge's labels and judge_raw for the sampled rows were NOT read before scoring (only aggregate label counts for the whole run had been seen); this file was written before the --handlabels command ran and was not revised afterwards.
